name: Gweda
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: only survey/subgrouping refs (Ross 1988, Tupper 2007 sociolinguistic survey); no phonological description of Gweda located

sources.citation: OLAC resources in and about the Gweda language [grw], combined catalog (as of 2024-07-03), via Internet Archive copy of language-archives.org/language/grw
sources.note: Catalog only: lists the Gweda OPD (49078, ONLINE) as the sole language description besides Glottolog; other SIL items are offline (Alphabet Development Worksheet 70428, trial spelling guide 'Gweda a Hiyava Ma Giluma Babana' 70580, wordlists 85578/85579, Galuwahi Dictionary 92796 Project VITAL 2005).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page gwed1239 (Gweda; alt. Garuwahi, Garuvahi)
sources.note: No descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); only Ross 1988 overview, Aleman 2001 survey, Tupper 2007, Ethnologue/UNESCO atlas entries.

sources.citation: Tupper, Ian. 2007. Endangered languages listing: GWEDA [grw]. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG. 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology; sociolinguistic vitality summary (26 speakers of 308 villagers in 2001), notes SOV with postpositions, lists wordlists (1973, 1997, 2001) held at SIL Ukarumpa and cites Aleman 2001 survey as unpublished.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic languages. Richmond: Curzon. (archive.org scanned text already held by the project)
sources.note: Garuwahi appears only in the Papuan Tip language listing (Are-Taupota group, between Taupota and Tawala); no description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Easton, Catherine. 2007. Discourses of orthography development: community-based practice in Milne Bay (P.N.G.). PhD thesis, School of Communication and Critical Enquiry, Faculty of Humanities and Social Science, La Trobe University, Bundoora (October 2007). [OPAL deposit 2020, doi:10.26181/5fb5bf5e92b5f]

tone.summary: Orthography-development thesis; Gweda gets segmental remarks only (areal 5-vowel system, lateral flap, s/t split). Nothing on tone; stress and village 'tune' (stress+intonation) left unstudied.

sources.citation: Heineman, Paul & Martin Knauber (consultants). 2001 [online 2012]. Gweda Organised Phonology Data (OPD). Ukarumpa: SIL PNG. 6 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives 49078.
